Standardise Measures for JSON Format

Source: R/json-support.R
boilerplate_standardise_measures_json.Rd

Enhanced version of boilerplate_standardise_measures that preserves JSON-compatible structure and ensures proper data types for JSON serialization.

Usage

boilerplate_standardise_measures_json(
  measures_db,
  add_missing_fields = TRUE,
  remove_extra_fields = FALSE,
  preserve_meta = TRUE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

measures_db

List. The measures database to standardise.

add_missing_fields

Logical. Add standard fields that are missing? Default is TRUE.

remove_extra_fields

Logical. Remove non-standard fields? Default is FALSE.

preserve_meta

Logical. Preserve metadata fields (those starting with underscore) in JSON? Default is TRUE.

quiet

Logical. Suppress messages? Default is FALSE.

Value

Standardised measures database with JSON-compatible structure

Details

This function ensures that measures are properly formatted for JSON storage:

  • Converts vectors to lists for JSON arrays

  • Preserves metadata fields (e.g., _meta, _created)

  • Ensures all standard fields are present (as NULL if missing)

  • Maintains hierarchical structure

Standard fields include: name, description, type, values, value_labels, range, unit, items, reference, keywords, waves, cutoffs, scoring, reverse_items, and subscales.

See also

boilerplate_standardise_measures, boilerplate_save_json

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Load and standardise measures
db <- boilerplate_import_json(category = "measures")
db$measures <- boilerplate_standardise_measures_json(
  db$measures,
  preserve_meta = TRUE
)

# Save standardised database
boilerplate_save_json(db, format = "json")
} # }
